For an account on America/Los_Angeles, a request at 03:00 UTC on 1 April 2027 is 20:00 on 31 March local time, so it is March usage and is billed on the March invoice.
[section: Invoice periods and billing timezones]

Anything that reports a month of usage uses the same rule: the monthly total on the Console usage page, the invoice, and the figure Support gives a customer for a month. Usage before March 2027 stays on UTC periods and is not re-cut.

## Late usage
Usage that reaches the warehouse after BD1 is not added to an issued invoice. It is billed on the next month's invoice as a separate line marked "prior-period usage" with the original dates, so a customer comparing a month's export to its invoice may see those requests a month later.

## Price changes
A price-book change applies to usage from the first period that starts on or after its effective date. Mid-period changes are not prorated unless the order form says so."}, {"chunk_id": "google_drive/shared_drives/finance/2027-close-calendar-and-invoice-periods.json#1", "title": "2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods", "source_type": "Drive doc", "status": "final", "date": "2027-02-22", "authority": "final Drive doc - official documentation", "section": "2/4", "text": "… Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |
[section: Monthly close calendar]

Contracted accounts invoiced in arrears follow the same calendar; prepaid commitments are drawn down on BD2.

## Invoice periods and billing timezones
Until February 2027 every invoice period ran on UTC. From March 2027 usage onward, an account's invoice period runs from midnight to midnight in the account's billing timezone (`billing_timezone` on the account record; UTC unless set). A request belongs to the billing month, and to the invoice line, in which its timestamp falls in that timezone. For an account on America/Los_Angeles, a request at 03:00 UTC on 1 April 2027 is 20:00 on 31 March local time, so it is March usage and is billed on the March invoice."}, {"chunk_id": "confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/support-console-record-format-changes-2027.json#2", "title": "Support Console: Record Format Changes (April 2027)", "source_type": "Confluence page", "status": "published", "date": "2027-03-29", "authority": "published Confluence page - official documentation", "section": "3/6", "text": "… insert or query that still sends `amount_cents` fails with an unknown-field error.
- Compare amounts as money, not as strings. `"90.00"` is less than `"250.00"` even though it sorts after it as text.
## Account field on writes
- On the writable tables (`cases`, `credit_notes`, `disputes`) the account field is now `billing_account_id`, on reads and writes. Its value is the account's `account_id`.
- A write or query on those tables that still sends `account_id` fails with an unknown-field error. Read-only tables keep `account_id`.

## Billing timezone
- Accounts have a `billing_timezone` (an IANA name such as `America/Los_Angeles`; `UTC` unless set).
- Which billing month and invoice line a request belongs to is set by Finance's invoice period rules; see Finance's 2027 Close Calendar and Invoice Periods (Finance shared drive)."}, {"chunk_id": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/usage-export-csv-columns-2026.json#0", "title": "Usage Export: CSV Columns and Filters", "source_type": "Confluence page", "status": "published", "date": "2026-05-14", "authority": "published Confluence page - official documentation", "section": "1/1", "text": "## Columns
`request_id`, `timestamp` (UTC), `model`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `billed_tokens`, `project`.

## Common reasons a customer's own total differs from the export
- A project filter left on.
- A local timezone used to cut the month.
- Counting `prompt_tokens` only.

This page explains the export file. It doesn't change how invoice disputes or export mismatches are handled; that is on the billing case routing page.

last_updated: 2026-05-14"}, {"chunk_id": "confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/batch-api-pricing-2027.json#0", "title": "Batch API Pricing (2027)", "source_type": "Confluence page", "status": "published", "date": "2027-01-20", "authority": "published Confluence page - official documentation", "section": "1/1", "text": "## Pricing
Batch API jobs are billed at 50% of the Hosted API per-token rate for the same model, with a completion window of 24 hours.

## How it shows on an invoice
Batch usage is billed on its own invoice lines, one per week, described as "Batch jobs, <start>-<end>". Each line links to the jobs it bills.

## Limits
- Up to 50,000 requests per job.
- Jobs that don't finish in 24 hours are cancelled; finished requests in a cancelled job are billed, unfinished ones are not.

last_updated: 2027-01-20"}, {"chunk_id": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/console-invoice-list-sort-order-2027.json#0", "title": "Known issue: Console invoice list sorts by issue date", "source_type": "Confluence page", "status": "published", "date": "2027-03-05", "authority": "published Confluence page - official documentation", "section": "1/1", "text": "## Symptom
The Console invoice list sorts by the date an invoice was issued, not the period it covers, so a re-issued invoice for an earlier month can appear at the top.

## Workaround
Use the period filter or read the period on each invoice. Amounts and lines are correct.

## Status
Fix planned for the Console release in May 2027.

For each marketplace (AWS, GCP) and each SKU/dimension:

- Gross billed amount (marketplace) vs gross revenue recognized (Redwood)
- Marketplace fees (per statement) vs accrued fees
- Net remittance vs cash received
- Open receivable balance vs “due from marketplace” aging based on remittance schedule

### Recommended workflow
1) Extract Redwood internal usage summary by marketplace entitlement
- Group by: marketplace (AWS/GCP), seller account, entitlement ID, SKU, dimension, day/month
